newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends moderately weaker, volume light.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends moderately weaker, volume light.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended lower on Monday for the fourth consecutive session, but scale-down industry buying prevented the March contract from breaking through major support, dealers said.
New York opened broadly weaker on the heels of sharp losses posted in London overnight. But after a wobbly start, the market stalled in the $1,352-1,354 range basis March.
Trade buying toward the lows helped to offset selling pressure from speculators, dealers said.
March delivery fell $8 a tonne on the day, to $1,354, ranging from $1,350, a key psychological level, to $1,358. Second-position May eased $5, to $1,380, while the outer months slipped $4 to $7.
On the charts, March would need to hold above $1,342 to look constructive, while resistance was pegged at $1,358-1,360, and then at $1,380-1,382.
"March has to get thru $1,380-1382 to do anything," said one trader.

Meanwhile, the latest arrivals data from Ivory Coast contained few surprises, traders said. Ivorian arrivals stood at around 400,000 tonnes by mid-December, exporters said Monday, down from 540,000 tonnes at this time last year.
While most analysts expect this year's crop to come in well below last year's record yield, traders said a clearer picture of the harvest will emerge as January shipments are posted.
Volume on the day reached 4,424 lots.

The CSCE will hold a shortened session on Tuesday, December 31, before New Year's Eve. Cocoa futures trading will close at 1200 EST/1700 GMT. The CSCE will be closed Wednesday, January 1, in observance of New Year's Day.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
